It's a blatant disregard for your job, Congress. Imagine you're living paycheck to paycheck. You've got the house payment, the car payment, and credit card bills. You've been living beyond your means and it's finally time to buckle down. Then somebody walks into the kitchen and says, "I want a new car." You'd say, "Have you lost your mind? Don't you see we're in debt?" In Washington, it's apparently, "Yeah, we'll consider it. Why not? We're already in debt." The Senate wants faster energy permits. I want to be able to sell power from my roof. The Senate voted 62 to 33 to pass bipartisan legislation aimed at speeding up permits for power plants, transmission lines, pipelines, and other major infrastructure. The bill also includes provisions intended to keep data center energy costs from falling on other customers. I want more generation. I'd prefer solar, wind, and nuclear, and I'd prefer to use less coal. What I really want to see is a grid where people can generate power on their own roofs, use what they need, and sell what they don't. If your house can make some of its own electricity, you save money and take some of the load off the grid. If you make more than you use, you should be able to get paid for it. Imagine doing that across the country. Millions of houses producing some electricity of their own, connected to a grid that can actually take it. That's good for people's bills, and I think it's good for national security. I'd like Congress to spend a little more time figuring out how to make that possible. The Labor Department changes the rules for independent contractors The Labor Department announced a final rule Thursday that changes how it determines whether someone is an employee or an independent contractor under federal labor law. It replaces the Biden-era standard and gives more weight to two questions. How much control does the company exercise over the worker? And how much ability does the worker have to make a profit or take a loss independently? The change could affect people in trucking, delivery, retail, healthcare, and app-based transportation. Business groups argue it gives companies and workers more flexibility. Workers' advocates worry that people treated as contractors could lose access to protections such as overtime and the minimum wage. Jamie Raskin wants official messages preserved. Give the government a way to do both. | | ---|---|--- Rep. Jamie Raskin is asking the Justice Department, FBI, Department of Homeland Security, ICE, and Bureau of Prisons to preserve official communications and determine whether government business was conducted through apps with disappearing messages. His concern is that official records may have been deleted. I get it. If you're talking about government business and the messages just disappear, what the hell were you talking about? There needs to be a record somebody can audit. I also get why people in government need to text privately. You're in the car, at an event, or sitting in one committee while another committee is meeting. You need to get a message to somebody without calling them or tracking them down in person. That's how people work now. If the conversation is sensitive, it needs to be secure. And I don't think every working conversation between a member of Congress and an FBI agent needs to be put out for everybody to read. So commission a government communications service. I don't know what it would cost. Say it costs $50 million to develop and $10 million a year to maintain. You'd be paying for officials to have a secure way to talk, with official messages preserved and available to people who have the authority to review them. Raskin is right to ask where the records went. I'd like the government to give people a way to communicate securely and keep the records in the first place. Russia launches a major attack on Ukraine Russia launched a large overnight missile and drone attack after Vladimir Putin vowed to retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the bridge linking occupied Crimea to Russia. At least eight people were killed. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia launched more than 400 drones and more than 110 missiles , targeting energy, railway, and other infrastructure. International Court of Justice finds Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya | | ---|---|--- The International Court of Justice ruled Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in northern Rakhine State. The court ordered Myanmar to take steps to allow people who fled to return safely, pay reparations, and prosecute those suspected of committing genocide. Coming this afternoon on The Angry Democrat I went to the mayors' panel the other night with the mayors of Berea, Brook Park, and Middleburg Heights. They talked about AI, public safety, the Browns coming to Brook Park, and what that could do to traffic across the region. I'll have the article out this afternoon. This is the kind of coverage I want to do more of. I want to go to these things, hear what people say in the room, and bring it back to you. If you're willing to help me build that, it's . **Friday, November 20, 2026 - **
_**Iran:** President Donald Trump says no decision on renewed Iran strikes amid Israeli pressure. Iranian Navy says another tanker caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz._
_**Palestine:** Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian in Nuseirat, wound several in Gaza City. Israeli settlers shoot Palestinian olive harvester, assault residents across the occupied West Bank. Israel imprisons 350 Palestinian children, over 2,000 arrested since October 2023. Israeli violence drives 70% of mental health cases among MSF patients in occupied West Bank._
_**Yemen:** Saudi-backed airstrikes kill 15 people, wound 14 in Yemen. Coalition starts operation targeting Hodeidah port and Sana'a; Ansarallah warns of strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports._
_**Lebanon:** Israeli airstrikes and shelling target towns across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire." Israeli military claims it struck Hezbollah weapons facility in Beqaa Valley._
_**U.S.:** Slotkin says she will back Van Hollen over Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. More House Democrats elected to leadership posts. Senate Republicans block Iran war powers resolution 48-51. Iran war costs rise to $48.3 billion. Centrist Democrats refuse to shut down government to end Iran war. Anthropic raises $93.5 billion in IPO, the largest ever. Trump reports 751 stock and bond trades in September, including Nvidia, L3Harris and General Dynamics. Army unit offers soldiers a four-day weekend to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" in exchange for reenlisting. NBC: NSA classified internal network still down for a third day, forcing some employees to work from home. FCC votes to bar Chinese telecom firms from direct access to U.S. phone numbers. USDA proposes limiting SNAP eligibility rule. Federal judge rules Agriculture Secretary violated the Constitution with Christian messages sent to department employees. Guardian: Attorney General's wife marketed supplements with unproven health claims. GAO: Pentagon lacks a department-wide plan to fix munitions shortages worsened by the Iran war. Army plans to detonate tons of toxic lead in Iowa._
_**International:** Thousands protest across Colombia against proposed tax changes and rising living costs. Iraq reaches compromise with Kataeb Hezbollah to set up joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar. Haitian police claim they killed 34 alleged gang members. Hasina supporters in Bangladesh clash with government. RSF seizes Blue Nile municipality. Nayib Bukele planning to run for a third term. Myanmar's government rejects ICJ genocide ruling as "unfair." Spanish court grants conditional bail to U.S. philanthropist James "Fergie" Chambers. South Korea's Supreme Court overturns former prime minister's 15-year sentence. Xi tells Trump the U.S. should do the "right thing" on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in ties._

# Iran
* **Trump says no decision on renewed Iran strikes amid Israeli pressure:** President Donald Trump [told](https://substack.com/redirect/6767d087-fcbd-4091-8bad-d729f5aa5ff9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Axios on Thursday that he would not decide on his next steps in the war against Iran until the new year. "I am not rushing into any decision [on Iran]. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year," Trump said, amid pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch a new bombing campaign. According to Axios, the White House has requested Pentagon and intelligence assessments of potential Iranian responses to several U.S. strike scenarios, including whether attacks could trigger Iranian strikes on Gulf oil and gas facilities.
* Mossad director Roman Gofman reportedly visited Washington and Miami last week to press for renewed attacks, presenting Israeli intelligence claims about Iranian chemical weapons development.
* **Iranian Navy says another tanker caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz:** Iran's Navy [said](https://substack.com/redirect/b00eb068-0e92-4007-ac02-b49f512c9668?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that an oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. According to the Navy, the vessel ignored warnings, switched off its navigation systems, and entered a prohibited area before hitting the mines.

# Palestine
* **Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian in Nuseirat, wound several in Gaza City:** An Israeli drone strike [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/98e17a94-8852-40f3-80a8-78601c588c99?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) one Palestinian north of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza early Friday, WAFA reported. Several Palestinians were wounded in another drone strike in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood.
* **Israeli settlers shoot Palestinian olive harvester, assault residents across the occupied West Bank:**
* **Ramallah:** Israeli settlers [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/2134e780-e62f-42a7-a93b-dfdd000a98be?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man in the back while attacking olive harvesters in Nabi Saleh on Friday, according to WAFA. Israeli forces also demolished a Palestinian home in the Harasha area of Al-Mazra'a Al-Gharbiya, while settlers dumped garbage at the entrance of a mosque in Burqa.
* **Bethlehem:** Settlers [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/db939976-7d08-4e05-a2ed-4beb7581f408?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) homes in Tuqu', smashing windows and damaging three vehicles. In al-Minya, settlers beat a Palestinian man and his wife with clubs and sprayed them with pepper spray.
* **Jericho:** Israeli forces [shot](https://substack.com/redirect/72d3207a-34e4-4d42-83f0-e9e9298f5fb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Palestinian man in the foot during a raid on the Bayader neighborhood.
* **Hebron:** Armed settlers [assaulted](https://substack.com/redirect/f3da910a-32f1-4394-a55c-37cf04c4e795?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) olive harvesters in Birin before Israeli forces arrested several Palestinians. Israeli soldiers also beat and injured a young man during a raid on Al-Fawwar refugee camp.
* **Israel imprisons 350 Palestinian children, over 2,000 arrested since October 2023:** Israeli authorities are holding approximately 350 Palestinian children in prisons under conditions involving torture, starvation, medical neglect, and deprivation of family visits and education, according to a joint statement by the Palestinian Prisoners' Society and the Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs marking World Children's Day. This excludes children detained in Gaza whose exact numbers remain unknown due to enforced disappearance and restrictions on visits. Dozens of children are held under administrative detention without charge or trial.
* The organizations also highlighted the death of Palestinian teenager Walid Ahmad in Megiddo Prison in March 2025, with an autopsy identifying starvation, dehydration, and other medical complications as contributing factors. Israeli authorities subsequently closed the investigation into his death without holding anyone accountable, the groups said.
* **Israeli violence drives 70% of mental health cases among MSF patients in occupied West Bank:** Violence accounted for approximately 70% of mental health cases treated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in the occupied West Bank between October 2022 and April 2026, according to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/898c492e-e01c-4a46-afe4-707437d7437a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Anxiety and depression-related symptoms represented roughly two-thirds of reported mental health conditions, as Palestinians faced escalating Israeli settler attacks, movement restrictions, home demolitions, and forced displacement.
* "People in the West Bank have little choice but to live under relentless settler attacks, institutional violence, and permanent threat," said MSF head of mission Filipe Ribeiro. Despite growing mental health needs, MSF said Israeli restrictions have forced it to close operations in Jenin and Tulkarem and sharply reduce medical services in Hebron and Nablus.

# Yemen
* **Saudi-backed airstrikes kill 15 people, wound 14 in Yemen:** Airstrikes killed 15 people and wounded 14 others in Yemen's port city of Mokha and Taiz province on Thursday, according to the Sana'a-based Health Ministry. A strike on a rest stop in Mokha killed 10 people and wounded nine, while another targeting road repair workers in Taiz killed five and wounded five. Authorities blamed Saudi-backed forces for the attacks.
* **Coalition starts operation targeting Hodeidah port and Sana 'a; Ansarallah warns of strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports: **The Saudi-led coalition [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/dd070cd9-b39b-435f-9b0c-cd2916b924b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a military operation to "neutralize sources of threats used to target civilians in Yemen and the Kingdom" on Friday, covering the Yemeni governorates of Saada, Taiz, and Sana'a--the Ansarallah-held capital. The coalition also targeted Yemen's Hodeidah port, claiming to have hit capabilities used in "smuggling operations and the transport of weapons," following an evacuation order issued three hours prior to the attack.
* Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree warned that the Red Sea ports of Jizan, King Fahd Industrial Port, Jeddah, and Yanbu would become targets if Hodeidah is bombed.
* Saree also threatened to strike Saudi's Shuqaiq power station "in the coming hours" in response to reported Saudi airstrikes on power stations in Saada and Mocha, and declared Riyadh's financial center a military target.
* The exchange of threats comes amid escalating hostilities, with Saudi Arabia reporting the interception of five drones and a ballistic missile on Friday.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli airstrikes and shelling target towns across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire":**
* **Nabatieh:** Israeli warplanes [carried out](https://substack.com/redirect/b8cba306-8a52-4863-add1-1a9a09e786bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) two successive airstrikes on Kfartabnit on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.
* **Bint Jbeil:** Israeli forces shelled the outskirts of Hadatha and opened machine-gun fire toward Wadi Baraachit.
* **Tyre (Sour):** Forces [shelled](https://substack.com/redirect/94024a83-5411-4e70-92c4-bc0f0e947dc7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Mansouri and Majdal Zoun.
* **Israeli military claims it struck Hezbollah weapons facility in Beqaa Valley:** The Israeli military [said](https://substack.com/redirect/c171117b-d276-4038-882f-ca39c2563bdd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it struck the entrances to a site allegedly used by Hezbollah for "missile production and weapons storage" in the Janta area of Lebanon's Beqaa Valley. The military said the site had been targeted several times during the war and that Hezbollah members were recently seen arriving there, prompting strikes "to prevent its restoration."

# U.S. News
* **Slotkin says she will back Van Hollen over Schumer for Senate Democratic leader:** Sen. **Elissa Slotkin**(D-Mich.)****[announced](https://substack.com/redirect/1b9fccfb-1f33-4063-92d0-fa8475636465?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a video Thursday that she would support Sen. **Chris Van Hollen**(D-Md.) over Sen. **Chuck Schumer**(D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. She had previously announced her opposition to Schumer without committing to an alternative. Slotkin likened the moment to the 2018 pressure from younger members that eventually led **Nancy Pelosi** to step down from leadership, and said voters want "not marginal change. Not small nibbling at the edges." She is the fifth caucus member to publicly back Van Hollen, who says he has about 15 public and private commitments, short of the 28 he needs in addition to his own vote.
* **More House Democrats elected to leadership posts:** Rep. **Debbie Dingell** (Mich.) won another term as DPCC chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, and Reps. **Maxwell Frost**(Fla.), **Sarah McBride**(Del.), a**nd Sydney Kamlager-Dove**(Calif.) were elected DPCC co-chairs on Thursday. Rep. **Morgan McGarvey** (Ky.) won the "caucus leadership representative" post, and Rep. **Kristen McDonald Rivet** (Mich.) was elected "battleground leadership representative." The incoming freshmen also elected "class co-presidents," including Reps.-elect **Dan Koh** (Mass.),**Donna Miller**(Ill.), and **Fred Wellman**(Mo.).
* **Senate Republicans block Iran war powers resolution 48-51:** Senate Republicans [voted down](https://substack.com/redirect/2f535085-fe65-4c11-a710-8cb8817c85d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) another war powers resolution on Thursday, which would have directed President Trump to end hostilities in Iran. Republican Sens. **Susan Collins**(Maine), **Lisa Murkowski**(Alaska) and Rand Paul (Ky.) joined almost the entire Democratic caucus in supporting the resolution; Sen. **John Fetterman**(Penn.) was the only Democrat to vote against the bill. Sen. **Thom Tillis** , who voted for a similar resolution in September, voted against this one. The House passed a complementary resolution 220-204 in mid-September, led by Rep. **Seth Moulton**(D-Mass.), with seven Republicans joining Democrats.
* **Iran war costs rise to $48.3 billion:** The Pentagon's **Arthur Miller** told Sen. **Richard Blumenthal** at a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing Thursday that the Iran war's cost had risen to $48.3 billion as of Nov. 13, up from just over $47 billion in October and excluding damages to U.S. military facilities in the Middle East. Blumenthal demanded that the Pentagon release estimates of the damage to U.S. bases.
* **Centrist Democrats refuse to shut down government to end Iran war:** Centrist Democrat Reps. **Brad Schneider**(D-Ill.)**,** **Scott Peters**(Calif.), and **Greg Landsman** (Ohio) [said](https://substack.com/redirect/d68f0fe0-5ab2-4a70-8d53-edb0377904e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday that they would not shut down the government to end the Iran war, despite increasing calls from the party's progressive wing to use all tools at their disposal. Federal funding is set to run out on Dec. 11, a little less than a month before the Democratic majority is sworn in on Jan. 3. Republicans will need a significant number of Democratic votes to pass a funding patch using a "fast-pass" vote, which requires a two-thirds majority.
* **Anthropic raises $93.5 billion in IPO, the largest ever** : Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its initial public offering, the company [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/16854c44-088a-4fb5-91b7-9caa8ea005fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Friday, with an estimated market value of $1.6 trillion. Anthropic shares [declined](https://substack.com/redirect/f682c438-0560-4031-b67e-91c5c9cf066a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) early Friday, Reuters reported, and were trading about 9% below Thursday's close. The previous record for an IPO was held by SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June.
* **Trump reports 751 stock and bond trades in September, including Nvidia, L3Harris and General Dynamics:** President Donald Trump made tens of millions of dollars in personal trades across 751 transactions in September, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/c20a23bc-782c-485f-8bee-a19f7809734b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to a Thursday filing with the Office of Government Ethics. One Nvidia trade, worth $100,000 to $250,000 on Sept. 2, came a day before the company announced its $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face. Trump sold L3Harris stock twice, the contractor blamed for the FAA upgrades behind last week's nationwide ground stop. He also bought General Dynamics stock two days after the Pentagon announced munitions deals with the firm, and added to holdings in SpaceX, Tesla, Palantir, and Intel, in which the government took a 10% stake during 2025. Some of his trades were reported past the 45-day STOCK Act deadline. The White House maintains that Trump has no say in the trades made in his name, and that all investment decisions are made by "independent managers."
* **Army unit offers soldiers a four-day weekend to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" in exchange for reenlisting:** 43 soldiers from the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia [re-enlisted](https://substack.com/redirect/f7dc6b0d-a033-4e0f-b8dc-20ab1b9e6a71?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for two to six more years of service in exchange for a four-day weekend to play the newly released "Grand Theft Auto VI" video game, Task & Purpose reported. An Army counselor pitched the idea to her battalion commander after seeing another Army counselor mention the idea on TikTok. The game, which was released on Thursday, has generated more than $1 billion in pre-order sales.
* **NBC: NSA classified internal network still down for a third day, forcing some employees to work from home:** An internal classified computer network used by the National Security Agency, down since Tuesday, [remained](https://substack.com/redirect/84c87045-e162-4810-b743-e41842cd9972?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) out Thursday, leading some of the agency's non-essential staff to work from home, according to NBC News. Sources told the outlet that the outage has not affected the NSA's electronic intelligence collection or cybersecurity work, though it did reportedly affect a Georgia site that handles Middle East signals intelligence.
* **FCC votes to bar Chinese telecom firms from direct access to U.S. phone numbers:** The Federal Communications Commission [voted](https://substack.com/redirect/15aa0f34-552a-4ef5-982a-2c68436ff898?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday to bar China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom, and other IP-enabled service providers from direct access to U.S. phone numbers, citing national security as a pretext. The FCC previously barred the three Chinese carriers from providing international telecom services to the U.S. The decision extends a broad Trump administration crackdown that includes last month's FCC vote to ban all Chinese labs from testing U.S. electronics starting in December 2028 and Hong Kong carrier HKT's agreement to halt U.S. operations by September 2027. Beijing has threatened "necessary countermeasures" if the U.S. "persists in acting unilaterally."
* **USDA proposes limiting SNAP eligibility rule:** A new rule [proposed](https://substack.com/redirect/4ffa99a0-2b21-4bc6-a216-6b7404542130?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Agriculture Department on Thursday would restrict "broad-based categorical eligibility," which lets families receiving certain public benefits automatically qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), a change that the USDA estimates could drop 6.3 million people from the program. Because SNAP recipients are automatically eligible for free school meals, the families of more than 1.7 million affected children would have to complete paperwork to keep them. If the paperwork is not completed, school districts end up being responsible for the costs of these meals. The second Trump administration has already stripped SNAP benefits from more than 5 million people.
* **Federal judge rules Agriculture Secretary violated the Constitution with Christian messages sent to department employees:** Judge Trina Thompson of the U.S. District Court in Northern California [ruled](https://substack.com/redirect/68eb7ed2-af6b-40dd-ad5f-b02be653aeaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins' Christmas and Easter emails to all department employees went "too far" and amounted to coercion in violation of the First Amendment's ban on laws "respecting an establishment of religion." Rollins' Christmas email included a reference to "our savior Jesus Christ, who came to free us from our sins and open the door to eternal life," and her Easter email called the resurrection "the greatest story ever told."
* **Guardian: Attorney General 's wife marketed supplements with unproven health claims: Kristine Blanche**, a licensed physician assistant and the wife of Attorney General **Todd Blanche** , peddles supplements on a section of her website [called](https://substack.com/redirect/376b75b8-d897-4d10-9023-47eabb2a3f4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "Dr. Blanche's personal dispensary," one of which she suggested could treat Epstein-Barr virus and another which she suggested could treat HPV, the Guardian reported. No FDA-approved drug treats Epstein-Barr, and the product itself does not claim to. Blanche also sells roughly $600 "Man Up" and "Girlfriend" cleanse programs and a $595 treatment claiming to boost men's testosterone. Blanche was appointed in April to the advisory council of the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, which has a $170 million annual budget.
* **GAO: Pentagon lacks a department-wide plan to fix munitions shortages worsened by the Iran war:** A Government Accountability Office report released Thursday [found](https://substack.com/redirect/f44e8236-a2e7-4de2-b405-442f6b3ffa5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the War Department has taken steps to grow its munitions inventory but "doesn't have an overarching plan that identifies long-term goals, strategies, or ways to measure its progress." The watchdog said the Pentagon has no dedicated office with authority over inventories, which makes it harder to know whether production efforts meet department-wide needs and leaves the military services "reactive to global events rather than driven by total requirements." The GAO said the 2026 conflict with Iran, which began Feb. 28, "only reinforced" the problem, noting reports that U.S. forces used at least 850 Tomahawks in the first month and that the Army used up "virtually all" of its long-range missile stockpile.
* **Army plans to detonate tons of toxic lead in Iowa:** The Army [rescheduled](https://substack.com/redirect/8e83184d-4854-439a-8bd5-091fa2bd70d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its plans to detonate 68 barrels of degrading, volatile lead explosive at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, announcing that it would carry out the explosion on Monday instead of Friday after public concern that the lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems. The Defense Department and EPA had [known](https://substack.com/redirect/88997241-65bb-4146-824e-de11544b7c68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) since at least April that the Army was holding the explosives, according to The Washington Sun, though several communities potentially affected by the explosion first became aware of it on Sunday as a result of a public advisory.

# Other International News
* **Thousands protest across Colombia against proposed tax changes and rising living costs:** In the second nationwide protest since he took office in August, trade unions, students, and opposition groups [marched](https://substack.com/redirect/8389bf6d-9b74-4d8c-84c5-9a88c49e3bff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in Bogota and other major cities Thursday against proposals to lower the income tax threshold, raise healthcare contributions, and cut corporate taxes. Under the plan, Colombians earning more than about $985 a month would pay income tax, down from the previous threshold of about $1,419. Former President Gustavo Petro urged Colombians to mobilize, while de la Espriella said peaceful protest is allowed but that he would not tolerate road blockades or "urban terrorism." Riot police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters in some cities.
* **Iraq reaches compromise with Kataeb Hezbollah to set up joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar:** Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/263309bb-37d7-4803-afa0-bcb6480fab78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) late Thursday that Iraqi security forces will open a joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, on Friday morning, defusing a standoff after the government announced plans to send in forces amid allegations that the Shia armed group Kataeb Hezbollah was smuggling oil. He said the new combined force will include an Iraqi army brigade, a federal police brigade, an energy police regiment to protect oil pipelines, and two brigades from the Popular Mobilization Forces, which are officially part of Iraq's security forces and include some Kataib Hezbollah fighters.
* **Haitian police claim they killed 34 alleged gang members:** Haiti's national police [said](https://substack.com/redirect/de9e3157-1eb0-4c45-a219-2f5b405c1517?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that a Thursday operation in the southern Port-au-Prince neighborhood of Martissant killed 34 alleged gang members without a single police or civilian casualty. The area is reportedly under the influence of the Gran Ravine, Ti Bwa, and 5 Segond gangs, which belong to the Viv Ansanm alliance that Washington has designated a terrorist organization. Police said the operation was run with the government's Task Force, which has used explosive drones supported by a private military contractor led by Blackwater founder Erik Prince. The UN estimates that more than 2,250 people were killed in security operations in the first nine months of the year, including more than 300 civilians.
* **Hasina supporters in Bangladesh clash with government:** Supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina [tried](https://substack.com/redirect/e51bbc90-663c-4cb2-a2f1-bae577a81700?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to shut down businesses and public transport in Bangladesh on Thursday, with success mostly in southern districts where her outlawed Awami League is strongest, ending a week of protests against the government's rejection of her request for a new passport that would allow her to return. Ninety-seven platoons of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh were deployed across the country, and Dhaka police arrested 107 suspected Awami League-linked people in 24 hours, including former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid. Police claimed protesters killed two members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Wednesday night, set the houses of two BNP lawmakers in Hasina's home district on fire, and burned at least six buses, pickup vans and a section of railway line. Interim leader Muhammad Yunus' ancestral home in Chattogram was also reportedly set on fire. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman blamed "the country across the border" (referring to India) for the unrest.
* **RSF seizes Blue Nile municipality:** The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces [said](https://substack.com/redirect/06bd102a-ed40-4f4e-bbbd-c0e4f03f43ac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday that forces of its Founding Sudan Alliance captured the strategic Bau locality in Sudan's Blue Nile State, leading thousands of residents to flee to Ed Domain. The RSF said it took the town after a fight with the Sudanese army, which claimed the RSF took the municipality without a fight. Fighting in Blue Nile has escalated since the RSF and an allied SPLM-N faction led by Abdelaziz al-Hilu launched an offensive early this year that captured Kurmuk and Geissan. Sudan's government accuses neighboring Ethiopia of letting the RSF launch cross-border operations from its territory into the state.
* **Nayib Bukele planning to run for a third term:** Right-wing Salvadoran President Bukele, 45, formally [registered](https://substack.com/redirect/f6bdb03d-0d94-47b8-8b7a-966b92e9d626?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday to run for a third presidential term. The Supreme Court overturned the country's ban on immediate re-election in 2021, and a 2025 constitutional amendment allowing a third term lengthened presidential terms from five to six years. Bukele's challengers in the February 2027 election include Maytee Iraheta of the right-wing Nationalist Republican Alliance and Rafael Aguirre of the left-wing FMLN. Bukele has overseen a "state of emergency," under which his security forces have arrested more than 1 percent of the country's population with little due process, according to rights groups.
* **Myanmar 's government rejects ICJ genocide ruling as "unfair": ** A spokesperson for Myanmar's military government [told](https://substack.com/redirect/60d326bc-14fe-49df-8d93-1a650820f40f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a news conference Friday that "our country was unjustly accused" of genocide against its Rohingya population, and that the ICJ's Friday decision "is not a unanimous decision by everyone; it is not fair." The ICJ ruled 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in its 2017 crackdown, including mass executions, widespread sexual violence, and the burning of hundreds of villages. China, which is allied with Myanmar's military government, joined Myanmar in its criticism on Friday, with a foreign ministry spokesperson saying that such rulings by the UN's top court are "not conducive to the settlement of disputes."
* **Spanish court grants conditional bail to U.S. philanthropist James "Fergie" Chambers**: A court in Spain [granted](https://substack.com/redirect/9a541ea1-1e10-40a6-8164-2580a4a35b47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) conditional bail to James "Fergie" Chambers, an American pro-Palestine philanthropist the U.S. accuses of money laundering in support of Hamas. Chambers left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday after being held in Spanish custody for nearly five months. His release follows U.S. authorities' acknowledgment of "substantial" and "unintentional" errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent's sworn statement supporting its extradition request. The court said the translation errors could delay a final extradition decision, and his lawyer said these "raise grave concerns that the evidence was manipulated." Chambers denies wrongdoing and has applied for political asylum in Spain.
* **South Korea 's Supreme Court overturns former prime minister's 15-year sentence: **South Korea's Supreme Court [overturned](https://substack.com/redirect/dc4bb498-5927-4e60-8a6e-239c476bc874?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence on Thursday. Han was one of several top officials sentenced over President Yoon Suk Yeol's December 2024 martial law declaration. On Friday, the court said it was difficult to establish whether Han intended to legitimize that declaration when he called a cabinet meeting in response to it, and sent the case back to the Seoul High Court for a retrial. Han, 77, was sentenced to 23 years in January for insurrection, which an appeals court reduced to 15 years in May.
* **Xi tells Trump the U.S. should do the "right thing" on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in ties**: Chinese President Xi Jinping [told](https://substack.com/redirect/1d34721c-c1b9-49ec-94ad-70084c91d6a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Trump during Thursday talks in Shenzhen that the U.S. should do "the right thing" with respect to Taiwan, according to Xinhua's readout from the meeting. It did not elaborate on this comment, nor did it mention U.S. arms sales to Taipei, which Beijing has repeatedly demanded Washington end. Xinhua called the meeting, the third between the two leaders this year, "positive and constructive" and said they agreed to formulate an action plan for their "constructive, strategically stable relationship."

Photo by Clarens Siffroy / AFP via Getty Images. Friday, November 20, 2026 - Iran: President Donald Trump says no decision on renewed Iran strikes amid Israeli pressure. Iranian Navy says another tanker caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz. Palestine: Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian in Nuseirat, wound several in Gaza City. Israeli violence drives 70% of mental health cases among MSF patients in occupied West Bank. Yemen: Saudi-backed airstrikes kill 15 people, wound 14 in Yemen. Coalition starts operation targeting Hodeidah port and Sana'a; Ansarallah warns of strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports. Lebanon: Israeli airstrikes and shelling target towns across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire." Israeli military claims it struck Hezbollah weapons facility in Beqaa Valley. U.S.: Slotkin says she will back Van Hollen over Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. More House Democrats elected to leadership posts. Senate Republicans block Iran war powers resolution 48-51. Iran war costs rise to $48.3 billion. Centrist Democrats refuse to shut down government to end Iran war. Anthropic raises $93.5 billion in IPO, the largest ever. Trump reports 751 stock and bond trades in September, including Nvidia, L3Harris and General Dynamics. Army unit offers soldiers a four-day weekend to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" in exchange for reenlisting. NBC: NSA classified internal network still down for a third day, forcing some employees to work from home. FCC votes to bar Chinese telecom firms from direct access to U.S. phone numbers. USDA proposes limiting SNAP eligibility rule. Federal judge rules Agriculture Secretary violated the Constitution with Christian messages sent to department employees. Guardian: Attorney General's wife marketed supplements with unproven health claims. GAO: Pentagon lacks a department-wide plan to fix munitions shortages worsened by the Iran war. Army plans to detonate tons of toxic lead in Iowa. International: Thousands protest across Colombia against proposed tax changes and rising living costs. Iraq reaches compromise with Kataeb Hezbollah to set up joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar. Haitian police claim they killed 34 alleged gang members. Hasina supporters in Bangladesh clash with government. RSF seizes Blue Nile municipality. Nayib Bukele planning to run for a third term. Myanmar's government rejects ICJ genocide ruling as "unfair." Spanish court grants conditional bail to U.S. philanthropist James "Fergie" Chambers. South Korea's Supreme Court overturns former prime minister's 15-year sentence. Xi tells Trump the U.S. should do the "right thing" on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in ties. Drop Site Daily will be on break next week, November 23 -27, for Thanksgiving. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Trump says no decision on renewed Iran strikes amid Israeli pressure: President Donald Trump Axios on Thursday that he would not decide on his next steps in the war against Iran until the new year. "I am not rushing into any decision [on Iran]. We will see what happens after the beginning of the year," Trump said, amid pressure from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to launch a new bombing campaign. According to Axios, the White House has requested Pentagon and intelligence assessments of potential Iranian responses to several U.S. strike scenarios, including whether attacks could trigger Iranian strikes on Gulf oil and gas facilities. Mossad director Roman Gofman reportedly visited Washington and Miami last week to press for renewed attacks, presenting Israeli intelligence claims about Iranian chemical weapons development. Iranian Navy says another tanker caught fire after striking mines in Hormuz: Iran's Navy Thursday that an oil tanker caught fire after striking naval mines in the eastern Strait of Hormuz. According to the Navy, the vessel ignored warnings, switched off its navigation systems, and entered a prohibited area before hitting the mines. Palestine Israeli attacks kill one Palestinian in Nuseirat, wound several in Gaza City: An Israeli drone strike one Palestinian north of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza early Friday, WAFA reported. Several Palestinians were wounded in another drone strike in Gaza City's Sabra neighborhood. Israeli settlers shoot Palestinian olive harvester, assault residents across the occupied West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli settlers a Palestinian man in the back while attacking olive harvesters in Nabi Saleh on Friday, according to WAFA. Israeli forces also demolished a Palestinian home in the Harasha area of Al-Mazra'a Al-Gharbiya, while settlers dumped garbage at the entrance of a mosque in Burqa. Bethlehem: Settlers homes in Tuqu', smashing windows and damaging three vehicles. In al-Minya, settlers beat a Palestinian man and his wife with clubs and sprayed them with pepper spray. Jericho: Israeli forces a Palestinian man in the foot during a raid on the Bayader neighborhood. Hebron: Armed settlers olive harvesters in Birin before Israeli forces arrested several Palestinians. Israeli soldiers also beat and injured a young man during a raid on Al-Fawwar refugee camp. Israel imprisons 350 Palestinian children, over 2,000 arrested since October 2023: Israeli authorities are holding approximately 350 Palestinian children in prisons under conditions involving torture, starvation, medical neglect, and deprivation of family visits and education, according to a joint statement by the Palestinian Prisoners' Society and the Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs marking World Children's Day. This excludes children detained in Gaza whose exact numbers remain unknown due to enforced disappearance and restrictions on visits. Dozens of children are held under administrative detention without charge or trial. The organizations also highlighted the death of Palestinian teenager Walid Ahmad in Megiddo Prison in March 2025, with an autopsy identifying starvation, dehydration, and other medical complications as contributing factors. Israeli authorities subsequently closed the investigation into his death without holding anyone accountable, the groups said. Israeli violence drives 70% of mental health cases among MSF patients in occupied West Bank: Violence accounted for approximately 70% of mental health cases treated by Doctors Without Borders (MSF) in the occupied West Bank between October 2022 and April 2026, according to a new . Anxiety and depression-related symptoms represented roughly two-thirds of reported mental health conditions, as Palestinians faced escalating Israeli settler attacks, movement restrictions, home demolitions, and forced displacement. "People in the West Bank have little choice but to live under relentless settler attacks, institutional violence, and permanent threat," said MSF head of mission Filipe Ribeiro. Despite growing mental health needs, MSF said Israeli restrictions have forced it to close operations in Jenin and Tulkarem and sharply reduce medical services in Hebron and Nablus. Yemen Saudi-backed airstrikes kill 15 people, wound 14 in Yemen: Airstrikes killed 15 people and wounded 14 others in Yemen's port city of Mokha and Taiz province on Thursday, according to the Sana'a-based Health Ministry. A strike on a rest stop in Mokha killed 10 people and wounded nine, while another targeting road repair workers in Taiz killed five and wounded five. Authorities blamed Saudi-backed forces for the attacks. Coalition starts operation targeting Hodeidah port and Sana 'a; Ansarallah warns of strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports: The Saudi-led coalition a military operation to "neutralize sources of threats used to target civilians in Yemen and the Kingdom" on Friday, covering the Yemeni governorates of Saada, Taiz, and Sana'a--the Ansarallah-held capital. The coalition also targeted Yemen's Hodeidah port, claiming to have hit capabilities used in "smuggling operations and the transport of weapons," following an evacuation order issued three hours prior to the attack. Ansarallah military spokesperson Yahya Saree warned that the Red Sea ports of Jizan, King Fahd Industrial Port, Jeddah, and Yanbu would become targets if Hodeidah is bombed. Saree also threatened to strike Saudi's Shuqaiq power station "in the coming hours" in response to reported Saudi airstrikes on power stations in Saada and Mocha, and declared Riyadh's financial center a military target. The exchange of threats comes amid escalating hostilities, with Saudi Arabia reporting the interception of five drones and a ballistic missile on Friday. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes and shelling target towns across southern Lebanon amid "ceasefire": Nabatieh: Israeli warplanes two successive airstrikes on Kfartabnit on Friday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Bint Jbeil: Israeli forces shelled the outskirts of Hadatha and opened machine-gun fire toward Wadi Baraachit. Tyre (Sour): Forces Mansouri and Majdal Zoun. Israeli military claims it struck Hezbollah weapons facility in Beqaa Valley: The Israeli military it struck the entrances to a site allegedly used by Hezbollah for "missile production and weapons storage" in the Janta area of Lebanon's Beqaa Valley. The military said the site had been targeted several times during the war and that Hezbollah members were recently seen arriving there, prompting strikes "to prevent its restoration." U.S. News Slotkin says she will back Van Hollen over Schumer for Senate Democratic leader: Sen. Elissa Slotkin(D-Mich.) in a video Thursday that she would support Sen. Chris Van Hollen(D-Md.) over Sen. Chuck Schumer(D-N.Y.) for Senate majority leader. She had previously announced her opposition to Schumer without committing to an alternative. Slotkin likened the moment to the 2018 pressure from younger members that eventually led Nancy Pelosi to step down from leadership, and said voters want "not marginal change. Not small nibbling at the edges." She is the fifth caucus member to publicly back Van Hollen, who says he has about 15 public and private commitments, short of the 28 he needs in addition to his own vote. More House Democrats elected to leadership posts: Rep. Debbie Dingell (Mich.) won another term as DPCC chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee, and Reps. Maxwell Frost(Fla.), Sarah McBride(Del.), and Sydney Kamlager-Dove(Calif.) were elected DPCC co-chairs on Thursday. Rep. Morgan McGarvey (Ky.) won the "caucus leadership representative" post, and Rep. Kristen McDonald Rivet (Mich.) was elected "battleground leadership representative." The incoming freshmen also elected "class co-presidents," including Reps.-elect Dan Koh (Mass.),Donna Miller(Ill.), and Fred Wellman(Mo.). Senate Republicans block Iran war powers resolution 48-51: Senate Republicans another war powers resolution on Thursday, which would have directed President Trump to end hostilities in Iran. Republican Sens. Susan Collins(Maine), Lisa Murkowski(Alaska) and Rand Paul (Ky.) joined almost the entire Democratic caucus in supporting the resolution; Sen. John Fetterman(Penn.) was the only Democrat to vote against the bill. Sen. Thom Tillis , who voted for a similar resolution in September, voted against this one. The House passed a complementary resolution 220-204 in mid-September, led by Rep. Seth Moulton(D-Mass.), with seven Republicans joining Democrats. Iran war costs rise to $48.3 billion: The Pentagon's Arthur Miller told Sen. Richard Blumenthal at a Senate Armed Services Committee hearing Thursday that the Iran war's cost had risen to $48.3 billion as of Nov. 13, up from just over $47 billion in October and excluding damages to U.S. military facilities in the Middle East. Blumenthal demanded that the Pentagon release estimates of the damage to U.S. bases. Centrist Democrats refuse to shut down government to end Iran war: Centrist Democrat Reps. Brad Schneider(D-Ill.), Scott Peters(Calif.), and Greg Landsman (Ohio) on Thursday that they would not shut down the government to end the Iran war, despite increasing calls from the party's progressive wing to use all tools at their disposal. Federal funding is set to run out on Dec. 11, a little less than a month before the Democratic majority is sworn in on Jan. 3. Republicans will need a significant number of Democratic votes to pass a funding patch using a "fast-pass" vote, which requires a two-thirds majority. Anthropic raises $93.5 billion in IPO, the largest ever : Anthropic raised $93.5 billion in its initial public offering, the company Friday, with an estimated market value of $1.6 trillion. Anthropic shares early Friday, Reuters reported, and were trading about 9% below Thursday's close. The previous record for an IPO was held by SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June. Trump reports 751 stock and bond trades in September, including Nvidia, L3Harris and General Dynamics: President Donald Trump made tens of millions of dollars in personal trades across 751 transactions in September, to a Thursday filing with the Office of Government Ethics. One Nvidia trade, worth $100,000 to $250,000 on Sept. 2, came a day before the company announced its $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face. Trump sold L3Harris stock twice, the contractor blamed for the FAA upgrades behind last week's nationwide ground stop. He also bought General Dynamics stock two days after the Pentagon announced munitions deals with the firm, and added to holdings in SpaceX, Tesla, Palantir, and Intel, in which the government took a 10% stake during 2025. Some of his trades were reported past the 45-day STOCK Act deadline. The White House maintains that Trump has no say in the trades made in his name, and that all investment decisions are made by "independent managers." Army unit offers soldiers a four-day weekend to play "Grand Theft Auto VI" in exchange for reenlisting: 43 soldiers from the 9th Brigade Engineer Battalion at Fort Stewart, Georgia for two to six more years of service in exchange for a four-day weekend to play the newly released "Grand Theft Auto VI" video game, Task & Purpose reported. An Army counselor pitched the idea to her battalion commander after seeing another Army counselor mention the idea on TikTok. The game, which was released on Thursday, has generated more than $1 billion in pre-order sales. NBC: NSA classified internal network still down for a third day, forcing some employees to work from home: An internal classified computer network used by the National Security Agency, down since Tuesday, out Thursday, leading some of the agency's non-essential staff to work from home, according to NBC News. Sources told the outlet that the outage has not affected the NSA's electronic intelligence collection or cybersecurity work, though it did reportedly affect a Georgia site that handles Middle East signals intelligence. FCC votes to bar Chinese telecom firms from direct access to U.S. phone numbers: The Federal Communications Commission Thursday to bar China Mobile, China Telecom, China Unicom, and other IP-enabled service providers from direct access to U.S. phone numbers, citing national security as a pretext. The FCC previously barred the three Chinese carriers from providing international telecom services to the U.S. The decision extends a broad Trump administration crackdown that includes last month's FCC vote to ban all Chinese labs from testing U.S. electronics starting in December 2028 and Hong Kong carrier HKT's agreement to halt U.S. operations by September 2027. Beijing has threatened "necessary countermeasures" if the U.S. "persists in acting unilaterally." USDA proposes limiting SNAP eligibility rule: A new rule by the Agriculture Department on Thursday would restrict "broad-based categorical eligibility," which lets families receiving certain public benefits automatically qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), a change that the USDA estimates could drop 6.3 million people from the program. Because SNAP recipients are automatically eligible for free school meals, the families of more than 1.7 million affected children would have to complete paperwork to keep them. If the paperwork is not completed, school districts end up being responsible for the costs of these meals. The second Trump administration has already stripped SNAP benefits from more than 5 million people. Federal judge rules Agriculture Secretary violated the Constitution with Christian messages sent to department employees: Judge Trina Thompson of the U.S. District Court in Northern California Thursday that Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins' Christmas and Easter emails to all department employees went "too far" and amounted to coercion in violation of the First Amendment's ban on laws "respecting an establishment of religion." Rollins' Christmas email included a reference to "our savior Jesus Christ, who came to free us from our sins and open the door to eternal life," and her Easter email called the resurrection "the greatest story ever told." Guardian: Attorney General 's wife marketed supplements with unproven health claims: Kristine Blanche, a licensed physician assistant and the wife of Attorney General Todd Blanche , peddles supplements on a section of her website "Dr. Blanche's personal dispensary," one of which she suggested could treat Epstein-Barr virus and another which she suggested could treat HPV, the Guardian reported. No FDA-approved drug treats Epstein-Barr, and the product itself does not claim to. Blanche also sells roughly $600 "Man Up" and "Girlfriend" cleanse programs and a $595 treatment claiming to boost men's testosterone. Blanche was appointed in April to the advisory council of the National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health, which has a $170 million annual budget. GAO: Pentagon lacks a department-wide plan to fix munitions shortages worsened by the Iran war: A Government Accountability Office report released Thursday the War Department has taken steps to grow its munitions inventory but "doesn't have an overarching plan that identifies long-term goals, strategies, or ways to measure its progress." The watchdog said the Pentagon has no dedicated office with authority over inventories, which makes it harder to know whether production efforts meet department-wide needs and leaves the military services "reactive to global events rather than driven by total requirements." The GAO said the 2026 conflict with Iran, which began Feb. 28, "only reinforced" the problem, noting reports that U.S. forces used at least 850 Tomahawks in the first month and that the Army used up "virtually all" of its long-range missile stockpile. Army plans to detonate tons of toxic lead in Iowa: The Army its plans to detonate 68 barrels of degrading, volatile lead explosive at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, announcing that it would carry out the explosion on Monday instead of Friday after public concern that the lead dust could cause environmental contamination and health problems. The Defense Department and EPA had since at least April that the Army was holding the explosives, according to The Washington Sun, though several communities potentially affected by the explosion first became aware of it on Sunday as a result of a public advisory. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News Thousands protest across Colombia against proposed tax changes and rising living costs: In the second nationwide protest since he took office in August, trade unions, students, and opposition groups in Bogota and other major cities Thursday against proposals to lower the income tax threshold, raise healthcare contributions, and cut corporate taxes. Under the plan, Colombians earning more than about $985 a month would pay income tax, down from the previous threshold of about $1,419. Former President Gustavo Petro urged Colombians to mobilize, while de la Espriella said peaceful protest is allowed but that he would not tolerate road blockades or "urban terrorism." Riot police used tear gas and water cannons against protesters in some cities. Iraq reaches compromise with Kataeb Hezbollah to set up joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar: Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi late Thursday that Iraqi security forces will open a joint operations center in Jurf al-Sakhar, south of Baghdad, on Friday morning, defusing a standoff after the government announced plans to send in forces amid allegations that the Shia armed group Kataeb Hezbollah was smuggling oil. He said the new combined force will include an Iraqi army brigade, a federal police brigade, an energy police regiment to protect oil pipelines, and two brigades from the Popular Mobilization Forces, which are officially part of Iraq's security forces and include some Kataib Hezbollah fighters. Haitian police claim they killed 34 alleged gang members: Haiti's national police that a Thursday operation in the southern Port-au-Prince neighborhood of Martissant killed 34 alleged gang members without a single police or civilian casualty. The area is reportedly under the influence of the Gran Ravine, Ti Bwa, and 5 Segond gangs, which belong to the Viv Ansanm alliance that Washington has designated a terrorist organization. Police said the operation was run with the government's Task Force, which has used explosive drones supported by a private military contractor led by Blackwater founder Erik Prince. The UN estimates that more than 2,250 people were killed in security operations in the first nine months of the year, including more than 300 civilians. Hasina supporters in Bangladesh clash with government: Supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to shut down businesses and public transport in Bangladesh on Thursday, with success mostly in southern districts where her outlawed Awami League is strongest, ending a week of protests against the government's rejection of her request for a new passport that would allow her to return. Ninety-seven platoons of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh were deployed across the country, and Dhaka police arrested 107 suspected Awami League-linked people in 24 hours, including former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid. Police claimed protesters killed two members of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party on Wednesday night, set the houses of two BNP lawmakers in Hasina's home district on fire, and burned at least six buses, pickup vans and a section of railway line. Interim leader Muhammad Yunus' ancestral home in Chattogram was also reportedly set on fire. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman blamed "the country across the border" (referring to India) for the unrest. RSF seizes Blue Nile municipality: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces Thursday that forces of its Founding Sudan Alliance captured the strategic Bau locality in Sudan's Blue Nile State, leading thousands of residents to flee to Ed Domain. The RSF said it took the town after a fight with the Sudanese army, which claimed the RSF took the municipality without a fight. Fighting in Blue Nile has escalated since the RSF and an allied SPLM-N faction led by Abdelaziz al-Hilu launched an offensive early this year that captured Kurmuk and Geissan. Sudan's government accuses neighboring Ethiopia of letting the RSF launch cross-border operations from its territory into the state. Nayib Bukele planning to run for a third term: Right-wing Salvadoran President Bukele, 45, formally on Thursday to run for a third presidential term. The Supreme Court overturned the country's ban on immediate re-election in 2021, and a 2025 constitutional amendment allowing a third term lengthened presidential terms from five to six years. Bukele's challengers in the February 2027 election include Maytee Iraheta of the right-wing Nationalist Republican Alliance and Rafael Aguirre of the left-wing FMLN. Bukele has overseen a "state of emergency," under which his security forces have arrested more than 1 percent of the country's population with little due process, according to rights groups. Myanmar 's government rejects ICJ genocide ruling as "unfair": A spokesperson for Myanmar's military government a news conference Friday that "our country was unjustly accused" of genocide against its Rohingya population, and that the ICJ's Friday decision "is not a unanimous decision by everyone; it is not fair." The ICJ ruled 9-6 on Thursday that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in its 2017 crackdown, including mass executions, widespread sexual violence, and the burning of hundreds of villages. China, which is allied with Myanmar's military government, joined Myanmar in its criticism on Friday, with a foreign ministry spokesperson saying that such rulings by the UN's top court are "not conducive to the settlement of disputes." Spanish court grants conditional bail to U.S. philanthropist James "Fergie" Chambers: A court in Spain conditional bail to James "Fergie" Chambers, an American pro-Palestine philanthropist the U.S. accuses of money laundering in support of Hamas. Chambers left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday after being held in Spanish custody for nearly five months. His release follows U.S. authorities' acknowledgment of "substantial" and "unintentional" errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent's sworn statement supporting its extradition request. The court said the translation errors could delay a final extradition decision, and his lawyer said these "raise grave concerns that the evidence was manipulated." Chambers denies wrongdoing and has applied for political asylum in Spain. South Korea 's Supreme Court overturns former prime minister's 15-year sentence: South Korea's Supreme Court former Prime Minister Han Duck-soo's 15-year prison sentence on Thursday. Han was one of several top officials sentenced over President Yoon Suk Yeol's December 2024 martial law declaration. On Friday, the court said it was difficult to establish whether Han intended to legitimize that declaration when he called a cabinet meeting in response to it, and sent the case back to the Seoul High Court for a retrial. Han, 77, was sentenced to 23 years in January for insurrection, which an appeals court reduced to 15 years in May. Xi tells Trump the U.S. should do the "right thing" on Taiwan to avoid setbacks in ties: Chinese President Xi Jinping Trump during Thursday talks in Shenzhen that the U.S. should do "the right thing" with respect to Taiwan, according to Xinhua's readout from the meeting. It did not elaborate on this comment, nor did it mention U.S. arms sales to Taipei, which Beijing has repeatedly demanded Washington end. Xinhua called the meeting, the third between the two leaders this year, "positive and constructive" and said they agreed to formulate an action plan for their "constructive, strategically stable relationship." | | ---|---|--- 📖 Israeli Diplomat Offered Iowa Attorney General Free Trip, Then Asked for Favors 🛒 for your Drop News/Not Bombs Hoodie 💬 our Whatsapp Broadcast Channel for the latest reporting, podcasts, and breaking news, delivered directly ⚠️ You can go to your to unsubscribe from the Drop Site Daily newsletter--while still getting the rest of our reporting Become a Drop Site News Paid Subscriber Drop Site News is reader-supported. Three men face federal drug charges after agents seized more than 200 marijuana plants and about 120 pounds of processed marijuana from a property in Embden, according to a criminal complaint filed Friday in U.S. District Court in Bangor.
Lester M. Fuentes Gonzalez, Hector A. Roque De Escobar and Osvaldo Guillermo Gamez Fernandez are each charged with conspiring to manufacture more than 100 marijuana plants and manufacturing more than 100 plants, including aiding and abetting that conduct.
All three men are described in court documents released Friday as Cuban citizens.
Tracking the communist drug cartels in our spare time... Subscribe to The Robinson Report
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..C1X2YrtmE1FxhG_1T7R0IgrccLh3xQLMcnpCcO6W980?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=225816477)
Federal agents searched the Barron Road property Thursday following an investigation into an alleged growing operation that authorities say had been operating since at least January, according to an affidavit by Homeland Security Investigations Special Agent Pierre Mathieu.
All three men were at the property when agents arrived, Mathieu wrote. Investigators found marijuana plants in the home's basement, a garage and an outbuilding. The processed marijuana was in the garage.
Agents also seized grow lights, heaters, cellphones and documents bearing Fuentes Gonzalez's name. Bags of discarded roots, stems and leaves indicated previous harvests, according to the affidavit.
Investigators used electricity records, an undercover visit and cellphone evidence to connect the men to the operation, Mathieu wrote.
Two electricity accounts in Fuentes Gonzalez's name had been opened in 2024. Records reviewed by investigators showed one account used well above 8,000 kilowatt-hours per month beginning in January, while the second averaged 5,515 kilowatt-hours per month. Mathieu described both accounts' consumption as substantially higher than typical household use.
During an interview conducted in Spanish after he was advised of his rights, Fuentes Gonzalez said the marijuana belonged to him, according to the affidavit. He also said he lived at the property and had arrived there a few days earlier.

Big news, friend! **My Democratic colleagues in the House have elected me to serve as our Battleground Leadership Representative for the next Congress!** Here’s what this role means: Members like me who represent the most competitive districts in the country, ones that can swing either way, get a representative who speaks for all of us directly to House Democratic leadership. Now, when decisions are made about what bills come to the floor, what fights we pick, and how we tell the country what we stand for, I’ll be at the table as the voice for districts like ours. And this year, that’s a lot of districts: more than 70, the largest class of battleground Democrats since this position was created. **Those 70+ seats are the reason Democrats have the majority. No battleground districts, no majority. It’s that simple.** And keeping that majority means proving to the voters who took a chance on us that they made the right call. Here in mid-Michigan, working families are doing everything right and still feeling the squeeze every month. They want real change that makes their lives better. My job is to bring that message to the leadership table and keep our focus on lowering costs and delivering results people can actually feel. name: Forward Party
subject: Utah Welcomes TWO New Independent Candidates to Its Capitol
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Forward Party and not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
Plus, join us for a BIG celebration.

| | | [ ](www.forwardparty.com)
---
The Salt Lake Tribune is [reporting](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=bFgHPJC2qbzXh_VTsyZga1HzQqIXpjaeOiFYIP8VEEmGLSc9lE4s0QEh6F772UP05POacTGsPUxo5mvnn8pIySogChvdVLKYcr7X8pdOKro&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_131a&n=1) on two independent state candidates winning seats in the state’s House of Representatives: “Sergio Sotelo, treasurer of a local electricians union, and Patrick Belmont, a Utah State University professor, won upset victories over GOP incumbents earlier this month. When the new lawmakers are sworn in early next year, Sotelo will represent the West Jordan area, and Belmont will represent part of Logan and Cache County.”
---
|
---
| We’ve shared the story of Utah State Senator and Forwardist, Emily Buss. Emily did not win her reelection bid, but she was close, losing her Utah Senate District 11 seat by only [122 votes](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=KO8ZOB0mq2gq63DvFrKfe8oCIZ93IyBvedKyU8y-WGSdksKO7k3EwvoVpZYuLdKFaMiW9g-qVC5AufKjJjx0INZYN5AKAyUyAI_C-AmKPoS6ER9wxYuMivP38LgYGnyjMImPb8w8txIVhKcYEzQAT-lI8c0pATd3flzbzk1mbX2DiXPKGcoEHyAjPoBY80Om&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_131a&n=2) — 40 shy of qualifying for a recount.

We at the Forward Party are incredibly proud of Emily’s service to Utah. As the highest ranking Forwardist serving in office in the entire country, Emily’s service stands as proof of concept that Americans are indeed hungry for greater competition at the polls, new leaders and new solutions. We can’t thank Emily enough for serving her community and as a pioneer in the Independent political movement. Where there was one, there are now two. We’re confident the trajectory of the Independent movement is alive and well.
---
**Forward Party CEO Makes the Case for More Political Competition on C-SPAN’s Washington Journal** **** Forward Party CEO, Lindsey Williams Drath, went on C-SPAN’s Washington Journal for a wide-ranging, [40-minute conversation](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=_KeSraPW0gSlxEBMOvJrEouH4SjeZmYtvTWulgNFAfYcg1l83BLlqN-eFbIf4JB-&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_131a&n=3) about the state of the Independent political movement. Watch or find clips of the conversation on [Instagram](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=HR9MoATtHgNjF_4kmlo5pGfhVYzNqviH6ZNxnUxs2AVl-3d5G9jD38QR4R85g9hb&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_131a&n=4). **Forward is Throwing a Party... Bring Your Purple Tie** **** On December 15th, we’re coming together (virtually) for the 2026 Forward End of Year Event: Virtual “For-Awards” Ceremony & Celebration. We’ll honor the volunteers, candidates and state teams who made this year possible and share our plans for 2027 and beyond. Want to join us on December 15th? [Register here](https://home.forwardparty.com/r?u=buF0JE9znb7uwvUkABWJkJE5nTfI3JdHDeOE2rB68pc&e=61868e7acdd36ae0ddf3e39aa8429171&utm_source=forwardparty&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=fast_forward_131a&n=5)

"My question is how is this going to work at all? Just walk me through the math..." Sorkin pressed Mamdani.
## [Watch Mamdani struggle when he's forced to answer a real question: ](https://substack.com/redirect/30e84f98-54a2-4312-8b94-9020fc0394fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/30e84f98-54a2-4312-8b94-9020fc0394fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/30e84f98-54a2-4312-8b94-9020fc0394fc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
# **Mamdani unveils plan to close Rikers, delays deadline to 2032**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani **[announced plans to close Rikers Island by 2032,](https://substack.com/redirect/fb0b5648-46a2-48cb-9c5a-aebc507cf9b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** pushing past the original legal deadline requiring replacement jails by 2027, fulfilling a long-held goal despite past criticism from President Trump and opposition from predecessor Eric Adams.
[| | | | | Townhall.com
---
@townhallcom
Socialist NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says he's closing Rikers Island and replacing it with four borough-based jails starting in 2029 that will "house thousands fewer New Yorkers." Mamdani: "Dignity for everyone means safety for everyone."
| 2:34 PM * Nov 20, 2026 * 4.6K Views18 Replies * 2 Reposts * 8 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/843865ba-02e4-4154-9b46-da09b4125bac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The plan hinges on reducing the jail 's roughly 6,000-person population** to about 4,500 through diversion programs, supervised early release, expanded housing and social services, and reinstating an online bail payment system, though funding sources remain unclear.
* **Rikers, a 413-acre complex between Queens and the Bronx known by nicknames like "Torture Island,"** has long drawn criticism over conditions; Mamdani called closing it a "legal and moral obligation" toward building a safer, more humane correctional system.

* * *
# **Mamdani arrested twice by NYPD unit he is now disbanding**
Mayor Zohran Mamdani's announcement disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group omitted his own history with the unit, which **[zip-tied and arrested him](https://substack.com/redirect/b8c94748-bc21-40d3-970b-fe2f37cda094?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during protests in 2021 and 2024, before he launched his mayoral campaign.
[| | | | | Fox News
---
@FoxNews
MUST WATCH: Resurfaced video shows Zohran Mamdani being arrested by the elite NYPD unit he's now disbanding, years before he became mayor. Members of the Strategic Response Group can be seen zip-tying activists, including Mamdani, during a Brooklyn protest in 2021. The ...
| 4:00 PM * Nov 20, 2026 * 24.8K Views33 Replies * 23 Reposts * 64 Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/6bb660e6-d346-4771-a6d9-aacb95191869?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The SRG will be folded into counterterrorism functions,** replaced by two new units -- a 30-officer First Amendment Support Team focused on de-escalation and a Patrol Support Division -- alongside new restrictions banning tactics like kettling, long guns, pepper spray, and tear gas against protesters.
* **Mamdani had publicly pledged to disband the unit back in December 2024** after his own arrest, fulfilling that promise Monday. Police Benevolent Association President Patrick Hendry criticized the move, saying Mamdani is prioritizing his "radical base" over public safety.

* * *
# **Hakeem Jeffries vows to investigate "MAGA extremists," including Musk**
Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries told MS Now host Jen Psaki that figures associated with **[the"MAGA extremist movement" should be prepared to answer questions](https://substack.com/redirect/c407b47a-94b4-4142-91d5-c4d5646976c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**, specifically discussing whether Elon Musk should face investigation.
[| | | | | Western Lensman
---
@WesternLensman
Psaki asks Jeffries if Elon is now trying to avoid congressional scrutiny and if he should be investigated. Jeffries says "EVERYONE who has been part of this MAGA extremist movement that has unleashed all of this carnage and damage on the American people, should be prepared to ...
| 2:39 AM * Nov 19, 2026 * 305K Views812 Replies * 533 Reposts * 1.8K Likes
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4b76c321-d043-45af-b85e-502281c3e27d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Jeffries previously framed Democrats ' midterm win as a mandate to "fight MAGA extremism,"** though the term remains undefined and could broadly apply to Trump administration policies supported by 2024 voters.
* **Musk has become a frequent target for Democrats since buying Twitter** and rebranding it as X, with critics citing his wealth, his platform changes, and SpaceX's federal contracts, even as some protesters have resorted to vandalizing Tesla dealerships in response.

* * *
# **Latest tech failure hits America 's farmers**
The USDA has experienced multiple system outages since Monday after its Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center **[detected a security incident,](https://substack.com/redirect/c58e3827-a233-42c3-86fc-508e0ccf3a9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** forcing a reset of database passwords and affecting farmer loan and financial aid programs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c58e3827-a233-42c3-86fc-508e0ccf3a9d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The disruption adds to a wave of recent tech outages nationwide** affecting banks, airlines, and other systems; Trump has dismissed the idea of a coordinated foreign cyberattack, calling the incidents isolated, even as the administration searches for a new national cyber director.
* **USDA officials gave conflicting explanations,** with one attributing outages to routine software updates while internal guidance warned staff of continued intermittent disruptions. A GAO report released the same week found the USDA has only partially met cybersecurity preparedness recommendations, warning of potential risks to the food supply.

Marsha Blackburn won the governor's office on November 3, and the headline writers treated it like a formality: first female governor in Tennessee history, Republican, done. But look one line down on the results table and you'll find the real story of this election. Blackburn took 45.5 percent of the vote -- a 2.6-point margin over Jerri Green, a Memphis city councilwoman, and the closest gubernatorial race in Tennessee since 1896. An independent businessman, David Hatley, finished at 9.3 percent, with a dozen more independents on the ballot behind him. Four years earlier, Bill Lee won this office by thirty points. The race shifted twenty-seven points toward the Democrats from the 2024 presidential baseline in a single cycle.
Something in the Tennessee electorate broke this month. The fracture line runs through the registration rolls, and it runs straight back to the moving trucks.
